title: Fluorescence microscopy with the marine heterotrophic flagellate Cafeteria roenbergensis
author: Monica Berjon-Otero
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.qjmduk6

steps.title: Optional reagent treatment
steps.instruction: If desired, dilute bacteria‑free Cafeteria roenbergensis cells to the required density and add the chosen reagent (e.g., L‑Azidohomoalanine) before proceeding with the microscopy workflow.

steps.title: Prepare cell suspension
steps.instruction: Aliquot 5 × 10⁶ cells into each 1.5 mL microfuge tube, centrifuge 5 min at 5,000 g, 20 °C, discard supernatant, resuspend the pellet in 500 µL of 4 % paraformaldehyde in 1× PBS, and incubate 20 min at 20 °C.

substeps.instruction: Aliquot 5 × 10⁶ cells per 1.5 mL tube.
Centrifuge 5 min at 5,000 g, 20 °C.
Discard supernatant.
Resuspend pellet in 500 µL 4 % PFA in 1× PBS.
Incubate 20 min at 20 °C.

steps.title: Fixation, wash and permeabilize
steps.instruction: Centrifuge 5 min at 7,000 g, 20 °C, resuspend pellet in 250 µL 1× PBS and store overnight at 4 °C if needed; next day centrifuge 5 min at 5,000 g, 20 °C, resuspend in 500 µL 0.5 % Triton X‑100 in 1× PBS and incubate 15 min at 20 °C.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge 5 min at 7,000 g, 20 °C.
Resuspend pellet in 250 µL 1× PBS and keep at 4 °C overnight (optional).
Next day centrifuge 5 min at 5,000 g, 20 °C.
Resuspend pellet in 500 µL 0.5 % Triton X‑100 in 1× PBS.
Incubate 15 min at 20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare filter‑support grids
steps.instruction: Clean the vacuum‑manifold filter‑support grids with pure ELGA/milliQ water and remove the water by vacuum; add a drop of ELGA water onto each grid, place a 0.45 µm Millipore support filter, add another drop of ELGA water, place a 0.2 µm, 25 mm Anodisc Whatman filter on top, and apply vacuum at 5–10 Hg to remove the water. If required, block or wash the filter with the appropriate solution and remove by vacuum.

substeps.instruction: Rinse grids with pure ELGA/milliQ water.
Apply vacuum to remove the rinse water.
Add one drop of ELGA water onto each grid.
Place a 0.45 µm Millipore support filter on the water drop.
Add a second drop of ELGA water on top of the Millipore filter.
Place a 0.2 µm, 25 mm Anodisc Whatman filter on the water drop.
Apply vacuum at 5–10 Hg to remove all water.
Optional: block or wash the filter with the required solution, then remove by vacuum.

steps.title: Apply cells to filter
steps.instruction: Place the permeabilized cell suspension onto the prepared Whatman filter, apply vacuum at 5–10 Hg to remove the permeabilization buffer and immobilize the cells, and perform any necessary blocking and washing steps as described above.

substeps.instruction: Dispense the cell suspension onto the Whatman filter.
Apply vacuum at 5–10 Hg to remove buffer and immobilize cells.
Perform required blocking and washing steps (if any).

steps.title: Stain on filter
steps.instruction: Transfer the filter with cells onto a piece of Parafilm, add the staining solution of interest and incubate according to the stain manufacturer’s instructions. Return the filter to the vacuum system and apply vacuum at 5–10 Hg to remove the staining buffer. If required, wash the filter with the appropriate buffer, optionally stain DNA with DAPI, SYBR or Hoechst, and finally apply vacuum at 5–10 Hg to remove any remaining liquid.

substeps.instruction: Place the filter on Parafilm.
Add staining solution and incubate as per manufacturer’s protocol.
Return filter to vacuum system and apply vacuum at 5–10 Hg to remove staining buffer.
Optional: wash filter with desired buffer.
Optional: incubate with DNA stain (DAPI, SYBR, Hoechst).
Apply vacuum at 5–10 Hg to remove remaining liquid.

steps.title: Mount sample for microscopy
steps.instruction: Add 10 µL of 70 % glycerol onto a glass slide, place the filter (cells facing up) onto the glycerol, add 10 µL of 70 % glycerol onto a coverslip, place the coverslip over the filter, apply gentle pressure for 20 min at room temperature, seal the coverslip edges with nail polish, and store at 4 °C or image immediately.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 µL 70 % glycerol to a glass slide.
Place the filter on the glycerol with cells facing up.
Add 10 µL 70 % glycerol to a coverslip.
Place the coverslip over the filter.
Apply pressure for 20 min at room temperature.
Seal coverslip edges with nail polish.
Store at 4 °C or proceed to microscopy immediately.
